why: Who owns a `send-message` effect once a turn hands it back. Ticket 26/09/09/PROCEDURAL-3D-END-TO-END: every `interactionSelect` completion left two of them in the browser console as `[DEBUG] wireEffectToFriendly: unmapped effect "send-message" dropped — unverified wasm-boundary conversion`, which read like lost work. It was not: `route_app_frame` (`⚛️reactor/🔄️turn/🦀️.rs`) wraps EVERY non-`UiPatch` `AppFrame` reply in `Effect::SendMessage{Shell{instance}}`, the reserved-tool-job completion turn parks them in `pendingTurnEffects`, and `invocationFromFrames` already applies them through `leftoverShellInvocationFrames` (the history patch the console logs one line later) before handing the SAME list to the friendly mapping. A shell or backbone send-message is transport with an owner; anything else has no host route at all and must stay loud.

cases.why: The `interactionSelect` shape: an AppFrame reply addressed at the calling instance. `shellFrameBytes` hands back its payload and the friendly mapping must stay silent.
`shellFrameBytes` declines a frame addressed elsewhere, but it is still transport owned by that other instance's own drain — never a friendly effect this instance should act on, and never a warning.
`routeHostEffects` already pushed this out the bound document port before the friendly mapping ran.
The real hole the old blanket drop was hiding: no consumer anywhere routes a topic-addressed message, so this one MUST stay loud.
A target-less send-message is malformed, not transport.
The default arm keeps its meaning: an effect kind with no case at all is still an honest, loud drop.
Control row — the new case must not shadow a real friendly projection.
